reason: The cited evidence shows that metastability engineering and TRIP effects are known in HEAs (E2) and that stress-induced phase transformations occur in related systems (E1), but neither passage directly addresses wear performance, the specific role of Al/Ti in CoCrFeMnNi coatings, or the claim that a harder transformation product reduces wear rates.
premises: Metastable phases in HEAs can undergo stress-induced transformation during deformation.
The TRIP effect (transformation-induced plasticity) can be engineered in HEAs by tuning composition to create metastability.
Stress-induced phase transformation leads to formation of a harder phase that accommodates strain.
The formation of a harder phase via TRIP reduces wear by mitigating material removal.
Increasing Al/Ti content can push an HEA coating near its phase stability limit to create the required metastable microstructure.
